headline: YOUR SCHOOL STILL OWNS ONE OF THESE.
sub: You can say no, in writing. The letter takes two minutes and the office has to keep it on file.
fact: 24,534 students paddled in US public schools in 2021-22. US Dept. of Education, Civil Rights Data Collection.
art: a single worn wooden school paddle with a taped handle lying on a plywood workbench in a garage, overhead view, soft window light, muted warm colors, documentary photograph

headline: 33 STATES STOPPED PADDLING. THEIR SCHOOLS ARE FINE.
sub: Kentucky's last district stopped in 2023. The state counted zero paddlings the next year.
fact: Kentucky Dept. of Education, 2023-24. 17 states still allow it; 15 still use it.
art: an empty green chalkboard in an old rural schoolroom with chalk dust and an eraser on the tray, wooden floor, afternoon light through tall windows, documentary photograph

headline: PRINT IT. SIGN IT. HAND IT TO THE OFFICE.
sub: A one-page letter that says no employee may hit your child. In every paddling state, the school has to honor it.
fact: Louisiana, Missouri and Florida now require your signature before a paddling; Texas and most others put the burden on you to say no.
art: a single sheet of white paper and a ballpoint pen on a wooden kitchen table beside a coffee mug, morning light, shallow depth of field, warm documentary photograph
